title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning regression and classification models often lack model uncertainty, while Bayesian models are computationally expensive. The paper proves dropout in neural networks is a Bayesian approximation to a deep Gaussian process and uses MC dropout stochastic forward passes to estimate predictive mean, variance, and log-likelihood. On regression benchmarks, MC dropout achieves lower RMSE and better predictive log-likelihood than VI and PBP on most datasets, e.g. Boston Housing test RMSE 2.97 over 20 splits.

match_target.why: User hint specifies Table 1 Boston Housing MC dropout RMSE in the 40-epoch x10 setting with 20 splits; this is the cheapest central predictive-performance result (506 samples) and directly shows dropout uncertainty improving RMSE relative to VI and PBP.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target metric is RMSE, an unbounded regression error, and the paper reports a standard error rather than a std over repeated runs, so the 10% relative band applies.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate predictions using MC dropout by averaging multiple stochastic forward passes through the trained dropout network.
requirements.quote: This is equivalent to performing T stochastic forward passes through the network and averaging the results.

requirements.stmt: Estimate predictive variance as the sample variance of stochastic forward passes plus the inverse model precision.
requirements.quote: which equals the sample variance of T stochastic forward passes through the NN plus the inverse model precision.

requirements.stmt: Use the model precision tau determined from the prior length-scale and weight decay.
Use Bayesian optimization over validation log-likelihood to find the optimal model precision tau.
requirements.quote: we use Bayesian optimisation (BO, (Snoek et al., 2012; Snoek & authors, 2015)) over validation log-likelihood to find optimal τ

requirements.stmt: Set the prior length-scale to 10^-2 for most regression datasets.
requirements.quote: set the prior length-scale to 10−2 for most datasets based on the range of the data.

requirements.stmt: Use small dropout probabilities, specifically 0.05 and 0.005, for the PBP-style small regression networks.
requirements.quote: We used dropout with probabilities 0.05 and 0.005 since the network size is very small

requirements.stmt: Train with Adam and mini-batches of size 32.
requirements.quote: Finally, we used mini-batches of size 32 and the Adam optimiser (Kingma & Ba, 2014).

requirements.stmt: Use 40 BO iterations to select parameters, then train the final model with 10x more iterations.
requirements.quote: The BO runs used 40 iterations following the original setup, but after finding the optimal parameter values we used 10x more iterations

requirements.stmt: Average reported results over 20 random data splits for the main regression benchmark.
requirements.quote: All experiments were averaged on 20 random splits of the data

requirements.stmt: The theoretical model corresponds to dropout applied before every weight layer in a deep NN.
requirements.quote: a neural network with arbitrary depth and non-linearities, with dropout applied before every weight layer

requirements.stmt: Estimate predictive log-likelihood by Monte Carlo integration of the dropout predictive distribution.
requirements.quote: We can estimate our predictive log-likelihood by Monte Carlo integration of eq. (2).
